items.followUp: State four characteristics of a suspension.

rubric.why: Gives the characteristic size range of colloidal particles.
rubric.description: Colloidal particles have a size between 1 nm and 1000 nm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the size range, including an equivalent range with units or clear endpoints.

rubric.why: Identifies the scattering of light by colloidal particles.
rubric.description: Colloids show the Tyndall effect: their particles scatter a beam of light.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the Tyndall effect or clearly stating that colloidal particles scatter light.

rubric.why: Identifies the characteristic random movement of colloidal particles.
rubric.description: Colloidal particles show continuous random (Brownian) motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Brownian movement or Brownian motion.

rubric.why: States that colloidal particles remain dispersed rather than settling on standing.
rubric.description: Colloidal particles do not settle down on standing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles remain suspended or do not settle.

modelAnswer: Colloidal particles have a size between 1 nm and 1000 nm.
They scatter light and show the Tyndall effect.
They show continuous random motion called Brownian motion.
They do not settle down on standing.

rubric.why: Identifies the physical properties or changes studied in physical chemistry.
rubric.description: Physical chemistry studies the physical properties and physical changes of matter.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning physical properties or physical changes of matter.

rubric.why: Identifies the laws or principles that explain those properties or changes.
rubric.description: It explains them using the laws and principles of chemistry and physics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the laws or principles governing matter.

modelAnswer: Physical chemistry is the branch of chemistry that studies the physical properties and physical changes of matter.
It explains them by applying the laws and principles of chemistry and physics.

items.followUp: Write the chemical formulae of carbon dioxide and common salt.

rubric.why: Gives the chemical formula of water.
rubric.description: The chemical formula of water is H₂O.

rubric.why: Gives the formula or chemical identity of common table sugar (sucrose).
rubric.description: The chemical formula of sugar (sucrose) is C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ or identifying the sugar as sucrose.

modelAnswer: The chemical formula of water is H₂O.
The chemical formula of sugar (sucrose) is C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.

items.followUp: Define a compound and give one example.

rubric.why: States that a mixture contains more than one substance or element.
rubric.description: A mixture contains two or more substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a mixture contains two or more substances or elements.

rubric.why: States that the components are not chemically combined or gives a valid example.
rubric.description: The substances in a mixture are physically combined, not chemically combined; air is an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the components are not chemically combined or for giving a valid example such as air or salt water.

modelAnswer: A mixture is a combination of two or more substances that are physically mixed and not chemically combined.
For example, air is a mixture of gases.

items.followUp: What is the nature of charge on protons?

rubric.why: Identifies the charge carried by cathode rays.
rubric.description: Cathode rays carry a negative charge.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that cathode rays are negatively charged.

items.followUp: How is nuclear fission used to generate electricity in a nuclear power plant?

rubric.why: Identifies U-235 as the fuel used in the process.
rubric.description: Uranium-235 is used as nuclear fuel.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying uranium-235 (U-235) as the fuel.

rubric.why: Describes the energy-producing process or its use to generate electricity.
rubric.description: Fission of U-235 releases heat, which produces steam to drive a turbine and generate electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning fission and energy release, or explaining that the heat produces steam that drives a turbine to generate electricity.

modelAnswer: Uranium-235 is used as fuel in a nuclear reactor.
Its nuclei undergo fission, releasing heat that produces steam; the steam drives a turbine connected to an electricity generator.

items.followUp: Define electron affinity and give one example of an element with high electron affinity.

rubric.why: States that electronegativity involves attraction for electrons.
rubric.description: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract electrons in a chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an atom attracts electrons.

rubric.why: Specifies that the attraction is for shared bonding electrons or gives a suitable example.
rubric.description: An atom attracts the shared pair of electrons in a covalent bond; for example, chlorine attracts the shared pair in H–Cl.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying shared or bonding electrons, or giving a suitable example such as chlorine in H–Cl.

modelAnswer: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.
For example, in H–Cl, chlorine attracts the shared electrons towards itself.

items.followUp: What is meant by effective nuclear charge?

rubric.why: Identifies inner-shell electrons as the source of shielding.
rubric.description: In a multi-electron atom, inner-shell electrons shield the outer electrons from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying inner-shell (core) electrons as the cause of shielding.

rubric.why: Explains that shielding reduces the nuclear attraction felt by outer electrons.
rubric.description: Shielding effect is the reduction in the nucleus's attractive force on outer-shell electrons due to inner-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that this shielding reduces the nuclear attraction experienced by outer electrons.

modelAnswer: The shielding effect is the reduction in the attractive force of the nucleus on the outer-shell electrons.
It is caused by the inner-shell electrons lying between the nucleus and the outer electrons.
